type.description: The message name — <name> in the routing key.

domain.description: The owning domain — <domain> in the routing key. Owned by the Windows State Manager; MTWindows is a Client publishing events in a domain it does not own.

kind.description: Which exchange carries this message. Never reaches the routing key.

ts.description: When the sender published this message, ISO-8601 UTC.

target.description: The WindowId reporting — the <target> routing segment. Required: a window speaks only for itself.

fallback.description: The DisplaySelectionFallbackMode the window carries — the whole closed set, so a consumer switches rather than string-matches. Always present: a normalized config has its kind default applied (screenWindow to offscreen, controlWindow to lastOther). 'offscreen' resolves to no display at all — a computed position beyond the rightmost one — while every other member names a display the chain found. Consumers key off this field, never off parsing reason.

reason.description: What was unsatisfiable and where the window actually landed, human-readable — for the tech the event exists to reach. Consumers key off fallback, never off parsing this text.

WindowDisplayUnsatisfied.description: A window's display plan named a panel that is not present, so the fallback chain placed it somewhere else. The chain always terminates, so the window is never left without a position — but it is not on the panel it was authored for, and this is the only place that says so.
